newsitem.title: USA: Meritage offers to buy Skyline Chili.
newsitem.headline: Meritage offers to buy Skyline Chili.

text.p: Meritage Hospitality Group Inc, a restaurant and hotel owner and operator, said Tuesday it recently made an offer to acquire Skyline Chili Inc
Skyline is a Cincinnati-based restaurant chain that owns and franchises about 95 Skyline Chili restaurants in Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana and Florida.
Meritage said its offer contains two options, the first involving a merger of the two companies whereby the existing majority shareholders of Skyline would receive $7.50 cash per share.

The remaining Skyline shareholders would receive stock of the consolidated company valued at $9.50 per Skyline share. At today's market value, that would be the equivalent of about 1.8 shares of Meritage stock for each Skyline share, it added.
The merger proposal is valued at about $34 million. Meritage said this option is designed to capitalize on certain tax advantages for those receiving stock.
It also contains provisions for additional Meritage stock to be issued if the value of the 1.8 Meritage shares received in the merger did not equal at least $10.50 within two years after the merger.
The second option involves a purchase by Meritage of newly issued Skyline stock equal to a majority of the outstanding stock for $9.50 cash per share, or about $32.3 million.
Skyline officials were not immediately available for comment.

In February, Skyline said it received an unsolicited offer from an unaffiliated third party to acquire or gain control of it. Skyline did not name the party at that time. Skyline said at the time its board formed a special committee to evaluate the offer.
In its statement issued today, Meritage said it made offers to Skyline's majority shareholders and its board in early and mid February.

"Combining the Skyline and Meritage businesses would create an exciting opportunity for the shareholders of both companies to participate in a larger and more diversified chain restaurant business," Christopher Hewett, Meritage president, said in a statement.
